text:
In ring-closing metathesis (RCM) the synthetic strategy is to:

1. “Cut” the target ring across the C=C bond that will be formed.  
2. Add a –CH₂ group to each of the two carbons that were originally involved in that C=C bond; this converts them into terminal alkenes (–CH=CH₂).  
3. The rest of the ring carbons remain in the same order, carrying the same substituents.

Target: 5-isopropyl-3,4-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene  
– Break the C1=C2 double bond.  
– Attach CH₂ groups to C1 and C2 to give two terminal alkenes.

Unfolding the ring now gives an eight-carbon chain (an octadiene):

CH₂=CH–C1–C6–C5(i-Pr)–C4(Me)–C3(Me)–C2–CH=CH₂

Number the chain from the left end to obtain the diene name:

C1  C2  C3  C4  C5  C6  C7  C8  
CH₂=CH–CH–CH–CH(i-Pr)–CH(Me)–CH(Me)–CH=CH₂  
 1     2     3         4            5         6         7   8

This is 4-isopropyl-5,6-dimethylocta-1,7-diene.

Among the given choices, that corresponds precisely to option (C).

Answer: C
